messages.subject: R crashing during CNV analysis
parts:
I've been using aroma affymetrix on a MacBook Pro and have several
issues:

1) I'm doing CNV analysis for 8 patients comparing each one to the
pool using affymetrix 6.0 data. I
can only do one chromosome for one sample at a time before R crashes
and I
have to force quit then restart the whole analysis. This is taking
forever! It seems to be something to do with generating the x0064 and
x00128 .png files and is worse for the big chromosomes than the
smaller ones.

2) I can't get the Chromosome Explorer to work - it opens if I launch
it
manually (not through R) but no data loads so I'm opening the .png
files
one by one.

3) No one I've asked seems to be able to tell me what
the result/plot actually means or how to interpret it properly. There
doesn't seem to be an explanation on your site either (I might have
missed
it!). Could you please add something to the documentation that
explains
the plot?

Any ideas/solutions would be appreciated.

Regards,

Rachel Burt


Session details below:
The software can get through the whole analysis if the files have
already been generated (as for chr16 here) but freezes when finishing
generating the files for a single chromosome of a single sample. That
is, if the analysis for chromosome 1 of sample 1 has been completed,
the program will move on and complete the analysis of chr1 of sample 2
but then freeze and not move on to sample 3 until R has been forced to
quit and the session restarted:

Hi Rachel,

I'll try to help you with your problems. I'll do it my replying to
each of them in a separate message. Although closely related, please
keep one topic per message as it is otherwise hard to keep track of
everything as the thread grows.

On Tue, Nov 11, 2008 at 8:23 PM, Rachel <bu...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
> I've been using aroma affymetrix on a MacBook Pro and have several
> issues:

I'd love to see your sessionInfo(); otherwise I have to 2nd guess what
packages and versions you have loaded. I can see though that you are
not using the lastest version of aroma.affymetrix, so please update
(see Page 'Installation, Updates & Patches' online). I will not do
any serious troubleshooting on old version.

>
> 1) I'm doing CNV analysis for 8 patients comparing each one to the
> pool using affymetrix 6.0 data. I
> can only do one chromosome for one sample at a time before R crashes
> and I
> have to force quit then restart the whole analysis. This is taking
> forever! It seems to be something to do with generating the x0064 and
> x00128 .png files and is worse for the big chromosomes than the
> smaller ones.
>

Yes, I think this the problems you are reporting (here and below) has
to with the generation of PNG files. The fact that you have problem
with x0064 and x00128 images and big chromosomes, which generate very
wide PNG images, indicates that there is a memory issue. This has
nothing to do with the package per se, but the PNG driver used.

In R, there are now several different graphical drivers that can be
used to generate PNGs and their performance and quality depends on the
operating system etc. From the verbose output, it looks to me that in
your case you are using the Cairo PNG device driver of the Cairo
package (there is now also a default Cairo driver in R), but to be
sure, what does:

> print(findPngDevice())

report. If you see something like:

function (...)
{
Cairo::CairoPNG(..., bg = NA)
}
<environment: 0x032903e4>

then you use the Cairo driver in the Cairo package. If so, then
thread 'ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks' (Aug 18, 2008) is useful; it
reports similar issues, identifies Cairo to be the cause, and suggests
two alternative PNG drivers: (i) the default png() of R and png2() or
R.utils. The person in that thread had problems with the former, but
success with the latter.

To use the png2() driver (PNG via postscript and ghostscript), do:

findPngDevice <- function(transparent=TRUE, ...) {
if (transparent) {
function(...) { png2(..., type = "pngalpha"); par(bg=NA); }
} else {
function(...) png2(...);
}
}

at the beginning of your script.

Let us know if this helps

Henrik

from your verbose output below I see that you are using the CbsModel
class for doing CN segmentation. This class is using the (fast)
Circular Binary Segmentation (CBS) method implemented in the DNAcopy
package and described in detail in the two CBS papers:

[1] Olshen, A. B.; Venkatraman, E. S.; Lucito, R. & Wigler, M.
Circular binary segmentation for the analysis of array-based DNA copy
number data. Biostatistics, 2004, 5, 557-572
[2] Venkatraman, E. S. & Olshen, A. B. A faster circular binary
segmentation algorithm for the analysis of array CGH data.
Bioinformatics, 2007

The 2nd is an follow up paper/improvement and that is what's
implemented in DNAcopy.

For interpretation of these results, I recommend reading these papers
and emailing the authors. The Bioconductor mailinglist is better
suited for discussing segmentation results in general. Although very
interesting, I will have very little time participating in such
discussion (unless I start developing my own methods).

If you wonder about the graphic annotation, then the horizontal blue
dashed lines are the CN levels for CN=1, CN=2, CN=3 on the log2-scale.
The cytoband on top is the same cytoband as generated by the 'GLAD'
(segmentation) package. Lavina Gordon made some comments on these in
thread '
Chromosome explorer - blue shades above ruler' (July 1, 2008):

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/75d289f449643151/f5238e2ecc6eef2c?lnk=gst&q=lavinia+blue#f5238e2ecc6eef2c

As with everything else on this group page, I/we welcome
contributions. It can be spell/grammar corrections, single sentences
or paragraphs or complete vignettes, and of course replies to
questions. Everything helps.

Hope this helps
